notes: v641 - all three rule sets rebuilt from the 1 August 2026 evidence session, and each one now carries its OWN entry and price band, because testing showed those cannot be separated from the exit. Defender: 15% target / 15% stop, $0.20-$0.99, made +45.7% with a 67.7% win rate. All-rounder: 20% target / 15% stop, $0.15-$1.75, made +69.5% at 62.5%. Hunter: a 20% TRAILING stop with NO take-profit and no fixed stop, $0.20-$0.99, made +145.5% at 50.8%. All three use the 5% dip entry, which beat buying at market in every band and every exit tested. Figures are the full ~2.9 years of stored history, $100k across 10 positions, top 4 a day at score 7+, after $3-a-side brokerage and slippage; random entries with the same trade count made about +27%. Hunter is the strongest and the hardest to hold: about half its trades lose, positions run about 50 days instead of days, and every winner gives back 20% from its peak on the way out. Stress-tested to 2% slippage it still returned +124.5%, its worst fall from a high was about 8%, and it spent 10 trades in a row below a previous high - that stretch is where rules get abandoned. The best-practice button now fills in Hunter. Honest caveat: the exits are well tested, but each band is the one that suited that exit best over ONE window on ONE market, so treat the bands as best-available rather than proven. Nothing changes for you automatically - open My Rules, tap a preset, review it, then Save. Practice money only. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
